Kronecker Factors: A1 (m1, n1), A2 (m2, n2) with Spectral Normalization self.A1 = nn.Parameter( _init_orthogonal_spectral((m1, n1), (m1, n1), device, dtype) ) self.A2 = nn.Parameter( _init_orthogonal_spectral((m2, n2), (m2, n2), device, dtype) ) # 3-Core Tensor-Train factors: G1, G2, G3 with Spectral Normalization self.G1 = nn.Parameter( _init_orthogonal_spectral( (1, tt_shapes[0], tt_ranks[1]), (tt_shapes[0], tt_ranks[1]), device, dtype ) ) self.G2 = nn.Parameter( _init_orthogonal_spectral( (tt_ranks[1], tt_shapes[1], tt_ranks[2]), (tt_ranks[1] * tt_shapes[1], tt_ranks[2]), device, dtype, ) ) self.G3 = nn.Parameter( _init_orthogonal_spectral( (tt_ranks[2], tt_shapes[2], 1), (tt_ranks[2], tt_shapes[2]), device, dtype ) ) # Direct symmetric LoRA bypass parameters self.lora_A = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros((self.lora_r, self.in_features), dtype=dtype, device=device)) self.lora_B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros((self.out_features, self.lora_r), dtype=dtype, device=device)) nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.lora_A, a=math.sqrt(5)) nn.init.zeros_(self.lora_B) @classmethod def factorize_dimensions(cls, in_f: int, out_f: int) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Auto-factorize input and output dimensions with shape padding.""" def best_factor_pair(dim: int) -> Tuple[int, int]: for d in range(int(math.isqrt(dim)), 0, -1
